title: What is the side of a square whose area is 441 square metres?
description: The video finds the side of a square from its area of four hundred forty one square metres, by trapping the square root between two tens and using the last digit. It then puts the side back into the area to check it.
teaching_notes: One idea: the side is the square root of the area, which we find by trapping it between two tens and using the last digit. Watch for students who test every number in turn, or who give the area instead of the side.

video_script.why: The child applies the method of the solved example, the side of a square is the square root of its area, and uses the trapping and last digit method to find it.
video_script.substitution: Trap the root between two tens, use the last digit to pick the candidates, and test them.
video_script.anchor: a square of area four hundred forty one square metres with its side marked by a question mark
video_script.payoff_line: The side of the square is twenty one metres
never_show: the answer before the answer beat
maths_rules: area of a square = side × side, so the side is √441
20² = 400 and 30² = 900, so the side is between 20 and 30
441 ends in 1, and 1² = 1 and 9² = 81 end in 1, so the side ends in 1 or 9: 21 or 29
ground: area 169: between 10 and 20; ends in 9, so the root ends in 3 or 7; 13² = 169
video_script.design: One idea: trap the side between two tens and use the last digit. The square stays in the anchor band and the candidates fill in on the working board.

narration: <bookmark mark='area'/>Step one, the area of a square is its side times its side.
<bookmark mark='root'/>The side is the number whose square is four hundred forty one.

beats.on_screen: 20² = 400 and 30² = 900; 441 lies between them; the side is between 20 and 30

marks.thirty: 30² = 900 is written and 441 is placed between them

narration: <bookmark mark='twenty'/>Step two, twenty squared is four hundred, and thirty squared is nine hundred.
<bookmark mark='thirty'/>Four hundred forty one lies between them, so the side is between twenty and thirty.

beats.on_screen: 441 ends in 1; 1² = 1 and 9² = 81 end in 1; the side ends in 1 or 9: 21 or 29

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Step three, the area ends in one. Only numbers ending in one or nine have squares ending in one.
<bookmark mark='nine'/>One times one is one, and nine times nine is eighty one.
<bookmark mark='cands'/>Between twenty and thirty, the side is then twenty one or twenty nine.

marks.try: 21 × 20 = 420 is written and 21 is added to make 441

narration: <bookmark mark='try'/>Step four, try twenty one. Twenty one times twenty is four hundred twenty, and one more twenty one makes four hundred forty one.
<bookmark mark='other'/>Twenty nine squared would be eight hundred forty one, which is too big.

beats.on_screen: check: side × side = 21 × 21 = 441 square m, the area given

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step five, put the answer back in the question. A side of twenty one gives an area of four hundred forty one square metres.
<bookmark mark='match'/>That is exactly the area we were given.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The side of the square is twenty one metres.
